qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dow possesses scale economies and low-cost feedstock integration via world-scale ethylene and polyethylene crackers on the US Gulf Coast and Western Canada. However, empirical capital efficiency confirms lack of an economic moat: 10-year median ROIC is only ~7.2% (falling to 6% in 2023-2024 and -1% in 2025). The company is an undifferentiated commodity price-taker whose margins fluctuate with global supply-demand swings and energy spreads, leaving it vulnerable to persistent Chinese capacity overbuild and European structural energy disadvantages.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 7.2% 10Y median vs 12% hurdle, REJECT). Dow is a cyclical commodity chemical producer selling undifferentiated polyethylene, ethylene oxide/glycol, and basic chemical intermediates. Despite world-scale US Gulf Coast integrated assets, it operates as a pure global price-taker subject to volatile feedstock spreads and Chinese overcapacity gluts. It cannot reliably price above inflation or generate double-digit returns on capital across the cycle (2023-2024 ROC 6%, 2025 ROC -1%, with 2025 FCF of -$1.42B).
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 7.2% fails the 12% hurdle. GAAP Net Income was $660M in 2023, $1,201M in 2024, and collapsed to a net loss of $(2,444)M in 2025. Free cash flow swung from $2,808M in 2023 to $(37)M in 2024 and $(1,417)M in 2025 due to heavy capital expenditures ($2.5B-$2.9B annually, including the Path2Zero net-zero project). Total long-term debt of $17.8B against $3.8B in cash leaves net debt at ~$14.0B. Operating segments: Packaging & Specialty Plastics (~50% of sales), Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure (~25%), Performance Materials & Coatings (~25%). Bulk commodity products lack switching costs and price at global spot parity.
